newsitem.title: USA: FAS's Schumacher to be USDA undersecretary - Senator.
newsitem.headline: FAS's Schumacher to be USDA undersecretary - Senator.

text.p: The Clinton administration will elevate Foreign Agriculture Service chief Gus Schumacher to one of the U.S. Agriculture Department's four top jobs, Senator Pat Roberts said Wednesday.

During a telephone news conference, Roberts said it was his understanding Schumacher would be nominated to be undersecretary for farm and foreign agricultural services. The post oversees the multibillion-dollar farm subsidy program and export promotion programs.
The Agriculture Department refused to comment. Schumacher was not immediately available for comment.

Roberts, Kansas Republican, told reporters he had some concerns about promoting Schumacher. Roberts said Schumacher, from Massachusetts, would face skeptical questions from Midwestern lawmakers about the 1988 presidential campaign of Democrat Michael Dukakis.
"He was author of the Belgian endive (as an) alternative crop," said Roberts, citing a remark lampooned by Republicans as proof that Democrats did not understand agriculture.
"I'm not trying to second-guess the secretary's appointment," Roberts said.
Before becoming head of FAS in 1993, Schumacher served stints at the World Bank and as the Massachusetts state agriculture director. At FAS, he has traveled widely to promote U.S. farm exports.
